note: v1, SO FAR: THE WHOLE SHAPE STANDING (the song I wanted to make; 4:42, 130 BPM, F). THE IDEA: take a number; halve it if it is even, treble it and add one if it is odd; go on until you reach one. Every number anyone has tried gets there and nobody has proved every number must. The song tries the first sixteen, in order, and plays each walk in full, end to end; nothing is repeated or cut to fit. A NUMBER IS THREE THINGS: its length (n sixteenths); its note (the n-th harmonic of the low F: 3 is C, 5 A, 7 E-flat, 9 G, 11 B, 13 D-flat), so a halving falls an octave in half the time; and its riff (its odd part written in twos, a stroke for a one and a rest for a nought, said round and round: 40, 20, 10, 5 is one phrase in half notes, quarters, eighths, sixteenths). Every walk ends alike: sixteen, eight, four, two, one, a ball coming to rest on F. The kit is outside the rule and keeps common time throughout. LISTEN FOR: 0:17.4, seven (288 sixteenths, eighteen bars exactly), where the second guitar joins; 2:06.7-2:28.2, twelve and thirteen on the ondes and the bass alone over a ride and a rim; 2:28.2, fourteen: seven said at half speed, then seven's whole walk again; 3:03.0, fifteen, eighty seconds long: it climbs to 160 (ten bars on one chord at 3:43) and the ondes, which plays each number at its true height, is out of sight from 3:43 to 4:11 and comes back from the top at 40; 4:26.7, the wheel four, two, one (one is not an end), fifteen turns of seven sixteenths, which is what brings it back to a bar line. THE BAND: two ct-twin guitars, ct-bass, ct-kit, and the library ondes Martenot as the lead. THE DRAW'S ROUND TYPE WAS instrument; on an empty slot the first round is the song, and the one instrument I set by measurement is the lead: 2.5 dB off each note per octave over middle C (a sine stood 2.5 dB under the band up high and 8.8 down low), its diffuser halved and 3 dB off at 350 Hz (it held 45% of 250-500 Hz; now 24%). MEASURED (seeds 0/11): 87.033 / 85.134; the first bare draft read 79.62 / 80.192. Against the eleven records 250-500 Hz reads 2.5 to 2.9 dB over in the long walks (4.2 in the opening on one guitar); everything else within 2.4 dB except 8-16 kHz in the climb (+3.5). The loud walks all sit within 1 dB of each other (-12.0 to -13.2 K); twelve and thirteen are 4 dB under. No card: nothing here needs his ear to go on. WHICH OF HIS RULES I TOOK AS BINDING: all of direction.rules; no words, so the vocal rules do not arise. Not heard by me.
next: It is bare, and anyone may build on it. In order of what I would do: (1) DYNAMICS: the loud walks are one level and one texture (variety is the weak term, 64-70): give nine, eleven and fifteen each a different kit feel and guitar register; fifteen's climb (3:03-3:43) should grow, and 160 should be the biggest thing in the song. (2) The opening seventeen seconds (one to six) are one guitar and a kick at full level: a real entrance. (3) The ondes: whether out of sight should be silence (as now) or something else is an ear's call; TOP in the generator is the top of the ribbon, TILT its level slope, --lead-gain its fader. (4) The second guitar's small phrase under 40, 80 and 160 could be a different sound. (5) 250-500 Hz is still 2.5-2.9 over: the guitars hold 30% of it (the album's 380 Hz cut is not on them here). Do not cut or repeat a walk to make the form tidier: that each takes as long as it takes is the song. --form prints where each walk starts.

v2, THE SUMMIT HAS ITS FALL INSIDE IT (chirper-three; section round, windows 8 and 9; the change is 3:43.2–4:10.9, the top of the fifteenth walk and its first step down). v1's note asked that 160 be the biggest thing in the song. Measured, it was the smallest of the loud stretches: ten bars on one chord, the left guitar striking twice and ringing for half of it, 1.9 dB under the long walks in the finished file. LISTEN FOR 3:43.2, the top: four guitars now, the new pair on the low A, a crash, the hands on the china; under the chord the bass no longer holds, it moves (A, a short F, A: a phrase two and a half bars long, said four times under the chord). 4:01.6, 80: the left guitar comes down to what the new pair is already playing. 4:10.9, 40: the new pair stops and the whole band is on the riff the bass has had since the top; the ondes comes back there as before.
THE IDEA: 160 is not one number. It is 80 doubled and 40 doubled twice, down to five: ONE phrase (stroke, rest, stroke) in six sizes, and from the top the walk does nothing but go down through them. v1 played two of the sizes at the top (the number's own, two bars a place, on the left guitar; the smallest, in sixteenths, on the right guitar and the kick). Now the sizes between are heard, each on what will have it next: TWO MORE GUITARS (the album's wall rig, new tracks wall-left and wall-right) say eighty's phrase, a bar a place, a storey under the number (A1, E2, A2); the BASS says forty's, half a bar a place, exactly as it plays it at 40. So at the top every chord of the next thirty seconds is already going, and the fall takes a storey off at a time. The kit's hands stay in common time, as v1 rules; the foot, which is in the rule, is lifted on the four of the new pair's six chords that it had played softly.
WHAT CHANGED: 18 notes on the two new tracks; the bass's six notes in 160 and 80 become eighteen; four kick strokes go from 0.78 to 0.95; the ride's 40 quarters in 160 are the china and one crash is added at 3:43.2. No walk is cut, repeated or moved, and no guitar, ondes or snare note changed.
WHAT I MEASURED (raw window on seed 0, then finished files on seeds 0 and 11). FIRST BENCH, not kept: the new pair at the album's setting (-3.5 dB, 3 dB off at 380 Hz) lifted 160 by 1.9 dB raw but put 3.3 dB into 250-500 Hz, where v1's note already reads the song 2.5 to 2.9 over the records. KEPT: the pair at -1 dB with 6 dB off at 380 Hz. Finished, 160 reads -13.89 -> -11.55 and -13.84 -> -11.63 dB (K; +2.3 and +2.2), and 80 reads -13.07 -> -11.52 and -11.50 (+1.6). THAT MAKES 160 LEVEL WITH THE LOUDEST STRETCH OF THE SONG, NOT OVER IT: the start of the fifteenth walk reads -11.54 and -11.64, the other long walks -12.0. It is the biggest by what is in it (four guitars, the low A, the china), and by half a decibel over seven, nine, eleven and fourteen. COST, benched raw at -2 dB on the pair (the kept setting is 1 dB up on that and was not benched for this): 160 carries 1.8 dB more of its level at 250-500 Hz than the walks either side (2.8 more in 80), and the china puts +4.5 dB at 8-16 kHz for those ten bars. Everything outside 3:43.2–4:10.9 is unchanged on both seeds (-66.5 dB residual or lower, 0.006 dB or less); the first half second of 40 differs by -44 dB (the pair's last chord ringing out). Loudness target -9.81 (was -10): at -10 every other bar came out 0.17 to 0.18 dB quieter.
SCORES 0/11: 87.033/85.134 -> 86.685/85.590 (-0.35, +0.46): kept on judgment. Variety rises on both seeds (70.4 -> 71.7, 64.6 -> 65.9). Structure falls on seed 0 (68.4 -> 65.3) and rises on seed 11 (64.0 -> 65.3): the scorer counts 21 sections where it wants at most 19, and on one of its seven cuts the count moved by one. -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP.

v7, THE NUMBERS ARE AT THEIR TRUE HEIGHT (whole song; 986 notes repitched, by up to 49 cents; none added, dropped, moved or changed in length or level). LISTEN FOR 0:17.4, the seventh walk: 7, 22, 11, 34, 17, 52, 26, 13. Each chord and each note of the ondes is now an overtone of the low string the band is chugging on; the sevens, elevens and thirteens are no longer the piano's notes. Then 2:14.4, thirteen on the ondes and the bass alone, where it is plainest. Not checked by ear, and this is a round an ear must judge: one card (below).
THE DRAW WAS A PALETTE ROUND. I took the song's whole palette of pitches and not one instrument: it is a choice, so I say so. The engine feature is new to the album (pitches as fractional key numbers).
WHY. The rule: "a number is the n-th harmonic of the low F", and the ondes "IS the number, at its true height". Until now every pitch was the semitone NEAREST the harmonic. That is 31 cents off for 7, 14 and 28; 49 off for 11 and 22; 41 for 13, 26 and 52; 45 for 35 and 70; 28 for 23 and 46; 27 for 53 and 106; 14 for 5 and all its doublings up to 160. Now every pitched note is the harmonic itself: the ondes at n times the low F exactly; the guitars' chord, the second pair's and the bass on the same harmonic brought down by octaves, with a pure fifth. The muted low-string strokes are the fundamental, as they were.
WHAT IT DOES TO THE WALK, and it is in v1's own words: "trebled-and-one it leaps up a twelfth AND A HAIR". In semitones the hair was a whole semitone or nothing, by the luck of the rounding (7 -> 22 a semitone, 11 -> 34 nothing, 13 -> 40 a semitone, 17 -> 52 nothing). True, it is one part in 3n: a tone at 3 -> 10, a semitone at 5 -> 16, then 80 cents at 7 -> 22, 63 at 9 -> 28, 52 at 11 -> 34, 44 at 13 -> 40, 38 at 15 -> 46, 34 at 17 -> 52, 25 at 23 -> 70, 16 at 35 -> 106, 11 at 53 -> 160. The bigger the number, the finer the hair; and a halving is a pure octave every time. The size of a number can be heard in the size of its step.
MEASURED (the pitched band alone, raw, seed 0). The ondes's line against the harmonic, for 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15: +13.7, +49.2, -40.9, +31.3, +11.8 cents before; 0.0, -0.3, -0.2, -0.1, 0.0 after. Finished file: every walk's level is within 0.10 dB (K) of v6's; -9.9 LUFS as before; the loudness target is not moved. What I looked for and did not find: a drop in roughness round the ondes's note (the level's wobble at 3 to 40 Hz there: 21.8% before, 20.0% after, over twenty numbers): the retuning is exact, but I cannot show by a meter that it sounds smoother.

WHAT I CANNOT KNOW, and it is the whole question: whether a power chord 49 cents under B over a low F reads as the string's own eleventh overtone or as a wrong note. On one fundamental the series is consonant in the way an alphorn or a throat singer is; to an ear set by the other sixteen songs it may only sound flat. --equal gives v6 back byte for byte.

WHY. A natural horn in F has no valves: its notes are the harmonics of its tube, and the tube of a horn in F sounds this song's low F (43.65 Hz). Its sixteen open notes ARE the song's first sixteen numbers, the seventh, eleventh, thirteenth and fourteenth as far off the keyboard as the tube makes them (Harry: 'True harmonics: keep them'). Now the horn sounds the walk's number as the walk begins and holds it to the end, with a new breath at every trebling (the leap) and at least every five bars.
